scams.name: Restaurant Racketeering & Minimum Spend
scams.description: St-Tropez restaurants have developed sophisticated systems to extract maximum spending. Restaurants compile secret databases tracking spending and tips - if you don't spend enough, you're blacklisted. Some demand €5,000 minimum or €1,500 per head for reservations. Despite included service charges, staff aggressively pressure for 'American-style' tips. One waiter chased a customer into the parking lot demanding an additional €500 tip. The mayor has condemned these practices as 'racketeering.'
scams.avoidance: Research restaurant policies and reviews before booking. Ask about minimum spending requirements upfront. Remember service charge is already included in France. Choose smaller local establishments over famous beach clubs.
scams.location: Beach clubs, high-end restaurants, Port area restaurants

scams.name: Luxury Watch Theft
scams.description: Organized criminal groups systematically target tourists wearing expensive watches (€100,000+). Spotters identify valuable timepieces, then communicate with thieves who steal the watch—subtly or violently—before escaping on mopeds with tampered plates. Three incidents in one weekend resulted in €400,000 worth of stolen watches. These thefts are increasingly brazen and sometimes violent.
scams.avoidance: Leave valuable watches worth over €5,000 at home. If wearing expensive watches, keep them covered. Stay aware of surroundings, especially near beach areas. Report suspicious behavior immediately.
scams.location: Pampelonne Beach, beach restaurants, Port area, yacht clubs, town center

scams.name: Villa Rental Fraud
scams.description: Scammers create attractive listings for luxury villas that don't exist or aren't theirs to rent. They use stolen photos, enticing descriptions, and below-market prices. Travelers pay via wire transfer, then arrive to find the property doesn't exist. Fake booking forms designed to look like Airbnb confirmations direct money to fraudulent accounts.
scams.avoidance: Use only established concierge services and rental agencies. Perform reverse image searches on property photos. Never pay via wire transfer—use credit card. Be suspicious of deals that seem too good to be true.

scams.name: Hotel Room Burglary
scams.description: Professional burglars target luxury hotel rooms, particularly those with terrace access. Two British women lost nearly €1 million—including 11 Hermès Birkin bags, Patek Philippe watches, Cartier jewelry—when their room was ransacked within hours of check-in. Thieves broke through the terrace door and tore the safe from the wall. A hotel employee was questioned, suggesting possible inside involvement.
scams.avoidance: Don't bring valuables worth more than €5,000. Request upper floor rooms without easy exterior access. Keep valuable items with you when possible. Consider travel insurance covering theft.
scams.location: Luxury hotels, villas with private terraces

scams.name: Gas Burglary (Villa Gassing)
scams.description: Criminals allegedly pump anesthetic gas through air conditioning vents or windows to sedate sleeping occupants before robbing them. Notable victims include F1 driver Jenson Button and TV presenter Richard Hammond. Police estimate 90% of villa raids go unreported. Medical experts dispute whether such 'knock-out gas' actually exists as described.
scams.avoidance: Choose upper floor accommodations. Lock all windows and terrace doors. Don't sleep with windows open. Consider portable door alarms.
scams.location: Rental villas, hotel rooms with external ventilation access

scams.name: Beach Club Overcharging
scams.description: Beach clubs employ questionable practices. Sun loungers cost €35-50 each. Famous clubs like Nikki Beach require €1,500 minimum spend on weekends. Despite websites stating service charges are included, staff express dissatisfaction with tip amounts. Getting weekend reservations at Club 55 may require 'tipping' waiters in advance.
scams.avoidance: Research prices and minimum spend before visiting. Ask for prices upfront before ordering. Remember service charge is already included. Consider less famous beach clubs.

scams.name: Boat/Yacht Rental Hidden Fees
scams.description: Boat rental companies advertise attractive daily rates but add hidden costs: fuel (St-Tropez has higher diesel prices), delivery/redelivery fees, mooring fees, water sports equipment. Captain fees vary—standard is €350 but some quote €500+. Additional charges appear for 'gourmet lunch' or mandatory insurance add-ons.
scams.avoidance: Get complete all-inclusive pricing in writing before booking. Compare total costs including fuel. Ask specifically about all potential additional charges.
scams.location: Port of St-Tropez, Marina, online booking platforms

scams.name: Pickpocketing & Distraction Theft
scams.description: Professional pickpockets operate in crowded tourist areas during summer. Organized gangs use distraction techniques—one causes a commotion while others target valuables. Some use the petition/clipboard approach. Scooter thieves may grab bags from pedestrians. Tuesday and Saturday markets at Place des Lices are high-risk.
scams.avoidance: Keep bags zipped and in front. Don't carry bags on street-side shoulder. Use money belts or hidden pouches. Be extra vigilant in crowded market areas.
scams.location: Place des Lices Market, Port area, crowded restaurants, beach areas

scams.name: Taxi Overcharging
scams.description: Unlicensed and some licensed taxi drivers target tourists with inflated fares. Common tactics: claiming meter is broken, taking long routes, forcing cash payment. Airport transfers from Nice to St-Tropez legitimately cost €240-275 (day) or €265-285 (night), but scammers quote much higher.
scams.avoidance: Use only official taxis from designated stands. Research standard fares before arrival. Use Uber for tracked journeys. Pre-book airport transfers through hotels.
scams.location: Nice Airport transfers, town center, beach areas

scams.name: Jet Ski Rental Damage Scam
scams.description: Some jet ski operators make false damage claims after rental. After you return the jet ski, they claim you damaged it and demand large sums—often under threats and coercion. If you refuse, you may be threatened with police where 'administrative charges' inflate the amount further.
scams.avoidance: Photograph/video the jet ski from all angles before rental. Ensure date/time stamps are visible. Never surrender passport as collateral. Research operators thoroughly.
scams.location: Beaches, water sports rental areas, Port Grimaud

scams.name: Contactless Card Skimming
scams.description: Thieves use digital skimming devices to steal from contactless-enabled cards without physical contact. They carry concealed readers that capture card information in crowded areas, allowing fraudulent purchases or card cloning.
scams.avoidance: Use RFID-blocking wallets or card sleeves. Keep cards in front pockets or secure inner pockets. Monitor card statements regularly. Set up transaction alerts.

scams.name: Fake Charity Petitions
scams.description: Scammers approach with clipboards asking for signatures for fake charities. While distracted reading and signing, an accomplice targets your bag or pockets. Even without theft, you may be pressured to donate to a non-existent cause.
scams.avoidance: Politely refuse and keep walking. Never stop to engage with clipboard wielders. Keep belongings secure if you do stop.
scams.location: Place des Lices, Port area, tourist walkways
